newsitem.title: UK: Bearish dollar writing on the charts, analysts say.
newsitem.headline: Bearish dollar writing on the charts, analysts say.

text.p: The dollar looks on the brink of a sharp technical downmove against the mark and the yen as key supports, trendlines and Fibonacci props lurk to tighten the screws on the U.S. currency, chartists said.

Against the mark, it must hold above 1.4970/50 marks, an area marking a former resistance line and a 61.8 percent retracement of the dollar's entire run-up from 1.4635 in late July to a 4 1/2 month high at 1.5455 on October 17.
Dollar/yen is fragile after dropping over two yen in less than 24 hours from around 114.
The erosion of 112 in European trade on Thursday signals a possible brush with psychological support at 110 yen in the near-term, analysts said.
A pyschological "round figure" support at 1.50 marks provided a interim cushion for dollar/mark.
"A fall below 1.50 marks wold set up a test of the key 1.4965/55 retracement, and it's crucial for the dollar to hold above," said Alan Dunne, technical analyst at Bank America.
The 1.4965 level is also significant because it was the breakout point for the dollar after its summer consolidation this year, said Dunne.
From there, the dollar climbed to the 4 1/2 month rally peak at 1.5455 in mid-October.
A break below the 1.4970/50 area would expose the dollar to the risk of sliding to 1.45 or even 1.44 marks, levels not seen since February of this year.
"A break below 1.4970 marks would be critical for the dollar," said Stuart Frost, market analyst at NatWest Markets.

A drop below 1.50 marks would also threaten other longer-term support levels. The dollar's 200-day moving average is currently at 1.5035 and a rising trendline in place for more than a year cuts in at 1.4925.

Dollar/yen has been on a slippery slope since slicing through support at 112.90 yen overnight. The downmove was exacerbated in European morning trading as 112 yen gave way for a test of key support at 111.75.
"The fall below 112.90 leaves a double top in place with a target to 111," said Dunne, adding the drop below 112 in European morning trade confirmed the 111 target.

Below 111, "there's pretty good support at 110.90, the low from October, ahead of the key pschological level at 110," said Dunne. The trigger for a dollar/mark recovery is the 1.5180 mark level, with more immediate resistance at 1.5080/1.51 marks. Dollar/yen would have to reconquer 112 yen soon to allow a retest of the 3 1/2 year high at 114.91, hit on October 29.
"As long as the dollar stays below 1.51 marks there is a risk for a move down to a key support zone at 1.4920/4880," said Dominique Corombelle, technical analyst at Generale Bank in Brussels.
"Only a highly unexpected move through 1.5180 could modify this view."
Medium-term, or three to six months ahead, the dollar still looks likely to go rally, analysts said.

"I would get really worried about that view though if the dollar dropped below trendline support at 108.30, while on dollar/mark the downside should be held by 1.4495, a trendline support drawn from April 1995," said Dunne. "Even if the downmove extends to those levels the dollar should be able to break higher again in the medium-term."
At 1146 GMT the dollar traded at 1.5070/77 marks and 111.80/90 yen compared with 1.5178/81 and 113.90/114.00 in late European trading on Wednesday.
